references.text: Jephthah had already sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites the first time, and now he sends them again to continue the negotiations
Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom to ask for permission to pass through their land, a similar diplomatic appeal as Jephthah makes here
Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, with a peaceful request, just as Jephthah sends messengers to the king of the Ammonites
Moses sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with words of peace, a parallel to Jephthah's diplomatic approach
Reference to earlier events where Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, which Jephthah uses as historical precedent
The wording 'continued' or 'again' shows repeated diplomatic effort, similar to what we see in other biblical texts
